name: Theranos
one_liner: Promised hundreds of lab tests from a few drops of finger-prick blood on its own Edison device.
story: Elizabeth Holmes's Theranos claimed its Edison device could run a full panel of lab tests from a finger-prick, reaching a ~$9B private valuation in 2014 and a Walgreens retail rollout. A WSJ investigation in October 2015 revealed the tech did not work as claimed, followed by CMS lab sanctions in 2016 and SEC charges in March 2018 alleging a fraud that raised over $700M from investors. The company dissolved in September 2018 and Holmes was later criminally convicted.

near_death.what: WSJ (John Carreyrou) October 2015 exposé reported Theranos's own device was unreliable and most tests ran on commercial analyzers
CMS sanctions after lab inspection; Holmes barred from operating a lab and Walgreens partnership unwound
SEC charged Theranos, Holmes and Balwani with 'massive fraud' in March; company dissolved in September

dismissed_by.who: Jina Choi, SEC San Francisco Regional Office director
dismissed_by.quote_or_fact: "The Theranos story is an important lesson for Silicon Valley"
Paraphrase: his October 2015 reporting showed Theranos ran most of its tests on modified third-party machines rather than its proprietary device, triggering the collapse.

name: Virgin Orbit
one_liner: Air-launched LauncherOne rockets from a modified Boeing 747 to put small satellites in orbit from anywhere.
story: Spun out of Branson's Virgin Galactic, Virgin Orbit bet that launching rockets from a 747 ('Cosmic Girl') would make small-satellite launch flexible and responsive, and it went public via SPAC in December 2021 at a $3.7B valuation (the SPAC deal value), though heavy redemptions left only ~$228M of an expected up to $483M. After spending more than $1B, its January 2023 mission from Cornwall (the first UK orbital attempt) failed, financing talks collapsed, and it filed Chapter 11 in April 2023. Its assets were auctioned in May 2023 for roughly $36M to Rocket Lab, Stratolaunch and Launcher/Vast.

near_death.what: First LauncherOne test flight failed to reach space on 25 May 2020
SPAC redemptions cut expected proceeds of up to $483M to about $228M
9 January 2023 launch from Spaceport Cornwall failed to reach orbit; operations suspended in March and Chapter 11 filed 4 April

name: Astra Space
one_liner: Aimed to build cheap, mass-produced small rockets for daily launches to orbit.
story: Astra promised low-cost rockets built like consumer products to enable daily launch, and in July 2021 became the first space launch company listed on Nasdaq via a SPAC merger with Craig McCaw's Holicity at a $2.1B deal valuation, with market value peaking near $3.9B (Bloomberg). Its small rocket reached orbit only twice amid repeated failures, and launches were paused after a June 2022 failure. In 2024 co-founders Chris Kemp and Adam London took it private for $0.50 per share, cut from a $1.50 proposal, when the board said the alternative was Chapter 7; market value had fallen to roughly $12M.

near_death.what: June 2022 launch failure (lost NASA TROPICS satellites) after earlier failures; rocket launches put on hiatus
Board special committee said the $0.50/share founder buyout was the only alternative to Chapter 7 bankruptcy; deal closed July 2024

dismissed_by.quote_or_fact: Paraphrase: TechCrunch labelled Astra's March 2024 take-private the space industry's first SPAC bust of 2024.
